slot.brief: Simple circuit diagram with one cell, its internal resistance and an external resistor; find terminal voltage or current, then power dissipated inside the cell.

stem: A cell of emf $12$ V and internal resistance $1\ \Omega$ is connected to a $5\ \Omega$ resistor as shown in the figure. What is the power dissipated in the cell's internal resistance?

verdicts.working: The total resistance is 5 + 1 = 6 Ω, so I = 12/6 = 2 A. Internal power = I²r = 2² × 1 = 4 W.

working:
$R_{\text{total}}=5+1=6\ \Omega$; $I=\dfrac{12}{6}=2$ A. $P_r=I^2r=(2)^2(1)=4$ W.

Independent check: The total resistance is 5 + 1 = 6 Ω, so I = 12/6 = 2 A. Internal power = I²r = 2² × 1 = 4 W.
solution:
The total resistance is $R=5+1=6\ \Omega$, so the current is $I=\dfrac{12}{6}=2\ \text{A}$. The power dissipated in the internal resistance is
$$P=I^2r=(2)^2(1)=4\ \text{W}.$$

figure.description: Draw one closed rectangular series loop. On the left branch, draw a cell with its positive terminal above its negative terminal, labelled emf 12 V. Show a series resistor labelled internal resistance r = 1 Ω. On the right branch, draw the external resistor labelled R = 5 Ω. Connect all elements in a single loop; no other components or wires.
